filed by the IO SI Sharvan Kumar.
FACTUAL POSITION AND PLEADINGS 2.

The brief facts relevant for disposal of the present DAR petition are that on 23.12.2017 at about 6:15 PM, the petitioner was standing with his friend Samir near Lal Akhada, in front of Chauhan Property Dealer when a car make 'Ecco' bearing registration no. DL- 2CAN-1282 (in short "offending vehicle") being driven by respondent no.1 in rash, negligent manner and high speed hit the petitioner.
The petitioner fell down and sustained injuries.
The driver of the offending vehicle started to flee away from the spot when Samir alongwith other pedestrians apprehended respondent no. 1 who disclosed his name as Rambir S/o Sh. Chandrapal Singh.
Thereafter, Samir called at 100 number.

Police took the petitioner to SGM Hospital for his medical examination and respondent no.
1 was also handed over to the police.
MACT Case No. 625/2018 (FIR no. 914/17) Aslam Ali v. Rambir & Ors.
Page no. 2 of 15 3.
It is stated that FIR bearing No. 914/2017 of PS Sultan Puri, u/s 279/338 IPC was registered in this regard.

4. After obtaining the copy of DAR, written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 and respondent no.2 and, it is, inter alia, submitted that the claim against them is based on false and fabricated story.
The offending vehicle has been falsely implicated in the present accident.
Accident was not caused by respondent no.1 but was caused due to the negligent driving of e-rickshaw by the petitioner at very high speed and in zig-zag manner.
There were many ditches on the road.
When the respondent no. 1 reached the T- point, the petitioner himself did not care for the vehicle and ramped the e-rickshaw in the offending vehicle.
It is also submitted that petitioner was not carrying a valid driving license at the time of accident.
The present claim has been filed only to extort money by the petitioner from the respondents and the same may be dismissed with cost.
5. Legal offer has been filed on behalf of respondent 3/insurance Company.
ISSUES 6.

After completion of pleadings, following issues were framed by this Tribunal on 23.04.2019: -
1.

Whether the petitioner Aslam S/o Mohd.
Hashim suffered injuries in road traffic accident occurred on 23.12.2017 at about 06:15 PM in front of Chauhan Property Dealer, Near Hazrilal Akhada, F-7, MACT Case No. 625/2018 (FIR no. 914/17)

In order to prove its case,
petitioner no.1 Aslam Ali has been examined as PW1, who has deposed in terms of his affidavit of evidence Ex. PW1/A and has relied on following documents:

8. Petitioner was cross-examined at length by Ld. Counsel for the Insurance Company wherein he submitted that there was no footpath on the road where he was standing.
After the accident, he was admitted twice in the hospital for one day.
Then for two days, 1- 2 months after the accident took place.

In the month of June 2017, he took admission in Netaji Subhash Institute of Technology for Civil Engineering but discontinued after 3 months due to MACT Case No. 625/2018 (FIR no.
914/17) Aslam Ali v. Rambir & Ors.
Page no. 4 of 15 registration issues.
Petitioner could not place on record the medical bills and certificates related to him playing volleyball as mentioned in his affidavit.
9. Dr. Nishchay Kaushik was examined as PW-2 brought the original disability certificate no. 1147 dated 20.07.2022 of the petitioner.
Dr. Nishchay identified the signatures of Dr. Prateek Garg who was Senior Resident in the Ortho Department at Dr. BSA Hospital.
During his cross-examination
, it was observed that as per the disability certificate, the petitioner can perform daily chores despite disability of 11 % in his left lower limb.
He can even drive properly and press the accelerator.
He can also use a tailoring machine with his left leg but can feel slight pain if excessive pressure is exerted.
He has suffered the present disability of 11 % due to treatment undergone by the petitioner in relation to the left lower limb due to which his bones have been malunited.
10. No evidence has been lead by respondent.

11. I have heard Ld. Counsel for the petitioner as well as respondent and have gone through the testimony of P W  1 a n d P W  2 including the pleadings and the documents.
My issue wise findings in the case are as under : ISSUE NO.1 1.

Whether the petitioner Aslam S/o Mohd. Hashim suffered injuries in road traffic accident occurred on 23.12.2017 at about 06:15 PM in front of MACT Case No. 625/2018 (FIR no. 914/17)
Aslam Ali v. Rambir & Ors.
Page no. 5 of 15 Chauhan Property Dealer, Near Hazrilal Akhada, F-7, Block Sultanpuri, Delhi due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle i.e. Ecco car bearing registration no. DL-2CAN-1282 which was being driven by driver Sh. Rambir S/o Sh. Chandra Pal on the said date, time and place?
OPP.
12.

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
13.

sentences.text: In order to prove this issue, the petitioner has examined himself as PW-1.

He deposed that on 23.12.2017 at about 6:00 to 6:30 PM, he was standing with his friend at Harilal Akhara, Near Chauhan Property Dealer and the offending vehicle bearing No. DL- MACT Case No. 625/2018 (FIR no. 914/17) Aslam Ali v. Rambir & Ors.
Page no. 6 of 15 2CAN-1282

coming from Nuri Masjid in very high speed and in negligent manner,
hit the petitioner in rash manner due to which the petitioner received grievous injuries.
He was taken to Sanjay Gandhi Memorial Hospital, Mangolpuri, Delhi with the help of his friend and other public persons where his MLC was prepared bearing no. 21409/17.
FIR No. 914/2017 was registered.

Petitioner has claimed a lump-sum amount of Rs. 50,00,000/-.
14.
The testimony of PW1 against the respondent no.1 is corroborated by the documentary evidence that respondent no.1 was present at the spot and driving the offending vehicle at the time of accident.

Keeping in view the facts & evidence produced by the petitioner, it has proved on record that the said accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle being driven by respondent no.1, as a result of which, the petitioner sustained injuries.

4 15.
The FIR has been lodged against the respondent no.1 and he has faced criminal charges of causing injuries by rash and negligent driving in the said accident.
16. In the MLC prepared in Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, it has been opined by the concerned doctor that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
There is pain, swelling and deformity in the left leg.

17. In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the rashness and negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle, which is MACT Case No.
625/2018 (FIR no. 914/17) Aslam Ali v. Rambir & Ors.
Page no. 7 of 15 clearly visible and as such, was responsible not only for this accident, but also for everything that followed thereafter including the cause of injuries sustained by the petitioner.
Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.
2. Whether the petitioner/ injured is entitled for compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?

OPP.
18.

As the issue no.1 has been proved in affirmative and in favour of the petitioner, the petitioner has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered in the above accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
19. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.

The pecuniary damages or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which she had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by her in the accident.

The non- pecuniary or general damages are those damages which are MACT Case No. 625/2018 (FIR no. 914/17) Aslam Ali v.
Rambir & Ors.
Page no. 8 of 15 incapable of being assessed which includes the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.

It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where she was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate her or to put her almost in the same place or position where she could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject like the judgment in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343.
20.

In light of the above legal propositions, the amount of compensation which could be considered to be 'just' in the opinion of this tribunal shall be as under:-

(i) Medical or Treatment Expenses 21.
As per his evidence, the petitioner has not placed any medical records/ bills on the judicial file.

In the absence of any medical documents, the petitioner is granted nominal amount of Rs. 10,000/-
under this head.
(ii) Pain and Suffering 22.

As per petitioner, he was under excruciating pain when MACT Case No. 625/2018 (FIR no.
914/17) Aslam Ali v. Rambir & Ors.
Page no. 9 of 15 the offending vehicle had hit him and he did not know who took him to the hospital.
As per MLC Ex. PW 1/2 petitioner suffered fracture of tibia and fibula in his left leg which was a grievous injury.
The Disability Certificate Ex. PW-2/1 reflects that the petitioner is a case of having of 11% Permanent Loco Motor Disability to his Left Lower Limb.

It is not possible to quantify the compensation admissible to injured for the shock, pain and sufferings etc. which he actually suffered because of the above injuries, but as stated above, an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by injured and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.
30,000/- is being awarded to him towards pain and sufferings during the said period of his treatment and immobility.
Thus, he is awarded a total amount of Rs. 30,000/- under this head.
(iii) Loss of Actual Earnings 23.
During the cross-examination of petitioner, he has deposed that at the relevant time, he was working part time at his father's tailor shop and was earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
Petitioner has not placed any document on record to prove his income.
There is no document on record to show that injured remained admitted in the hospital or was unable to do his daily work or to earn his livelihood.
Injuries sustained by injured were grievous in nature.

In the absence of any evidence as to the vocation MACT Case No. 625/2018 (FIR no. 914/17) Aslam Ali v. Rambir & Ors.
Page no. 10 of 15 or monthly earnings of the petitioner, it would be appropriate that the monthly income of petitioner be assessed as per the minimum wages payable to an unskilled person in Delhi as on the date of accident.
As per relevant notification, the minimum wages admissible to a unskilled person as on 23.12.2017 in Delhi were Rs. 13,584/.

As such, the petitioner is held entitled to one month wages i.e. Rs. 13,584/. The said sum is awarded to the petitioner under this head.
(iv) Loss of future earnings due to disability 24.
Petitioner claims in his affidavit Ex. PW1/A that he could not do his work due to accident.
Even after recovery he is unable to do his work efficiently.

However, as observed earlier, the petitioner has not been able to prove the nature of his vocation/ employment and therefore, the monthly income of the petitioner has been assumed as per minimum wages admissible to an unskilled person.

Admittedly, as per disability certificate of the petitioner, he has suffered 11% permanent physical Aslam Ali vs Sh. Rambir on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162561777/
6 impairment with respect to his left lower limb.
The above disability would definitely lower/ reduce the employability of any unskilled person and thereby hamper his earning capacity.
In the absence of any material to the contrary, it would be appropriate to hold that the functional disability of petitioner be assessed at 6.0%.
This Tribunal has already assumed the monthly income of petitioner to be Rs.13,584/- at the relevant time.

As far as the age of petitioner at the time of accident is concerned, the photocopies of petitioner's Aadhar Card which is Ex.
MACT Case No. 625/2018 (FIR no. 914/17) Aslam Ali v. Rambir & Ors.
Page no. 11 of 15 PW1/1; as per which documents, the year of birth of petitioner is 1999.
By calculation, the age of petitioner as on the date of accident i.e. 23.12.2017 was 18 years.

Therefore, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.,(2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a recent judgment dated 31.10.2017 given in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, the multiplier of '18' is held applicable for calculating the loss of future earnings of petitioner arising out of her above disability.

LIABILITY 27.

As already stated above, R-1 being the driver and principal tortfeasor and R-2 being owner of the offending vehicle, and also being vicariously liable for the acts of R-1, are jointly and severally liable to pay the awarded amount of compensation to petitioner.
However, since the offending vehicle was insured with R-3 at the time of accident, therefore, R-3 is liable to indemnify R-2 in respect of above liability.

As such R-3 is directed to deposit the above award amount within 30 days from the date of this Award by way of NEFT or RTGS mode in the account of this Tribunal under intimation to the petitioner/ injured and this Tribunal in terms of the format for remittance of compensation as provided in Divisional Manager Vs. In the absence of any evidence as to the vocation MACT Case No. 625/2018 (FIR no. 914/17) Aslam Ali v. Rambir & Ors.
Page no. 10 of 15 or monthly earnings of the petitioner, it would be appropriate that the monthly income of petitioner be assessed as per the minimum wages payable to an unskilled person in Delhi as on the date of accident.
The above disability would definitely lower/ reduce the employability of any unskilled person and thereby hamper his earning capacity.
In the absence of any material to the contrary, it would be appropriate to hold that the functional disability of petitioner be assessed at 6.0%.
The petitioner is also entitled to future prospects as per the observations made by a Three Judge Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Erudhaya Priya Vs. State Express Transport Corporation Ltd., MANU/SC/0545/2020 [please see para 7 (b)].
